channel.title: Runlet
channel.description: Runlet releases (stable and beta) for in-app updates.

item.title: Runlet 0.6.0
item.description:
- Eloquent models display in a Values view showing attributes, relations, and changes (marked with a dot) without running code; switch to Object view to see the whole object. - Driver casters let your project define how custom types display in results and dumps. - The documentation moved to runletapp.dev/docs with screenshots and image zoom. - Tab renaming focuses the field immediately with the whole title selected.
## Install or update
- **With 0.4.0 or later:** use **Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…** and choose **Install and Relaunch**. - **New install, or 0.3.0 and older:** download the DMG, drag Runlet to Applications, and open it. It's ad-hoc signed, so the first time go to System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security and click **Open Anyway**.
Runlet runs on macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later, on Apple silicon and Intel.
## What changed
- **Eloquent models in Values view** Shows attributes and loaded relations without running code, with marks for changed attributes. Switch to Object view to see the full structure. (#307) - **Driver casters** Project drivers can define how custom types display in results and dumps. (#6) - **Documentation website** Moved to runletapp.dev/docs with screenshots, dark mode, search, and click-to-zoom. (#287) - **Tab renaming** Renaming a tab focuses the field immediately with the title selected, ready to type. (#285) - **Development:** Claude drafts in release.sh run without user hooks. (#283)
The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/v0.6.0/CHANGELOG.md). `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums.
Crash logs: `Runlet-0.6.0-dSYMs.zip` has the symbols ([how to use them](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/main/docs/crash-logs.md)).

item.title: Runlet 0.5.0
item.description:
Pin any tab to keep it at the top of the tab bar when other tabs open and close. Pinned tabs stay open when you use Close Other Tabs or Close Tabs to the Right. Access pinning from the tab's context menu, the Window menu, the command palette, or Open Anything.
## Install or update
- **With 0.4.0 or later:** use **Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…** and choose **Install and Relaunch**. - **New install, or 0.3.0 and older:** download the DMG, drag Runlet to Applications, and open it. It's ad-hoc signed, so the first time go to System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security and click **Open Anyway**.
Runlet runs on macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later, on Apple silicon and Intel.
## What changed
- **Pinned tabs** Pin any tab to keep it at the top of the tab bar when other tabs open and close. Pinned tabs stay open when you use Close Other Tabs or Close Tabs to the Right. (#279) - **Development:** the changelog process now uses separate files per pull request to avoid conflicts (#277), and debug tools for testing pinned tabs are available.
The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/v0.5.0/CHANGELOG.md). `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums.
Crash logs: `Runlet-0.5.0-dSYMs.zip` has the symbols ([how to use them](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/main/docs/crash-logs.md)).

item.title: Runlet 0.4.5
item.description:
- ⌘W now closes the sheet or window in front, not the project tab behind it. - The Logs window shows a project driver's log files without opening the Commands panel first. - Debug builds now run as Runlet Dev with their own Dock icon, data folder, and settings.
## Install or update
- **With 0.4.0 or later:** use **Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…** and choose **Install and Relaunch**. - **New install, or 0.3.0 and older:** download the DMG, drag Runlet to Applications, and open it. It's ad-hoc signed, so the first time go to System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security and click **Open Anyway**.
Runlet runs on macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later, on Apple silicon and Intel.
## What changed
- **⌘W closes the sheet or window in front, not the editor tab behind it.** Using ⌘W in a sheet or another window now closes that sheet or window instead of the editor tab behind it. (#273) - **Logs shows a project's log files without opening Commands first.** When a project's log paths aren't known, the Logs window offers to load them on demand, letting you view logs without opening the Commands panel. (#271) - **Xcode Debug builds are now Runlet Dev.** Debug builds have their own bundle ID, name, icon with a DEV badge, and data folder. You can run the development build alongside the installed release without interference. (#267, #269)
The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/v0.4.5/CHANGELOG.md). `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums.
Crash logs: `Runlet-0.4.5-dSYMs.zip` has the symbols ([how to use them](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/main/docs/crash-logs.md)).

item.title: Runlet 0.4.4
item.description:
Runlet 0.4.4 includes a `scripts/release.sh` script that guides through the full release process: updating versions, creating changelog entries, and publishing GitHub releases and appcast updates. The script supports `--dry-run` to preview changes, `--claude` to draft release notes, and saves progress so you can stop and continue later. Use `clean <tag>` to remove files leftover from a release.
Filip.
## Install or update
- **With 0.4.0 or later:** use **Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…** and choose **Install and Relaunch**. - **New install, or 0.3.0 and older:** download the DMG, drag Runlet to Applications, and open it. It's ad-hoc signed, so the first time go to System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security and click **Open Anyway**.
Runlet runs on macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later, on Apple silicon and Intel.
## What changed
- **`scripts/release.sh`** guides you through a full release: preparing (creating a branch, updating versions, writing changelog) and publishing (creating tags, building packages, updating GitHub and appcast). It asks for confirmation before making external changes. (#263) - **Release script options**: use `--dry-run` to preview all changes, `--claude` to draft your changelog and release notes, and `clean <tag>` to remove leftover files. Progress is saved so you can stop and continue a release later. (#263) - Development: `WhatsNewTests` no longer break when you add new releases; a new test also verifies that the newest entry is complete.
The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/v0.4.4/CHANGELOG.md). `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums.
Crash logs: `Runlet-0.4.4-dSYMs.zip` has the symbols ([how to use them](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/main/docs/crash-logs.md)).

item.title: Runlet 0.4.3
item.description:
Runlet 0.4.3 is a small fix release.
## Install or update
- **With 0.4.0 or later** (or 0.4.0 beta 7 or 8): use **Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…** and choose **Install and Relaunch**. - **With 0.3.0 or older, or a new install:** download the DMG, drag Runlet to Applications, and open it. It's ad-hoc signed, so the first time go to System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security and click **Open Anyway**, or run `/usr/bin/xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Runlet.app`. From then on Runlet updates itself.
Runlet runs on macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later, on Apple silicon and Intel.
## What changed
- **Profiles window.** With no profiles yet, its buttons show their full labels. They read "New Docker Pr…" and "Import SSH Ho…" on macOS 15 and 26. In the remote folder browser, "Back to <path>" now shortens a long path in its middle, and "Try Again" always shows in full. - **Crash logs.** Stable releases now publish their debugging symbols, `Runlet-<version>-dSYMs.zip`. One command turns a Runlet crash report into function names, files and lines: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filipac/runlet/main/scripts/symbolicate-crash.sh | sh`. It needs Xcode's command line tools.
The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/v0.4.3/CHANGELOG.md). `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums of the zip, the DMG and the dSYMs.
Crash logs: `Runlet-0.4.3-dSYMs.zip` has the symbols ([how to use them](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/main/docs/crash-logs.md)).

item.title: Runlet 0.4.2
item.description:
Runlet 0.4.2 is the same app as 0.4.1, about **70 MB smaller**.
## Install or update
- **With 0.4.0 or 0.4.1** (or 0.4.0 beta 7 or 8): use **Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…** and choose **Install and Relaunch**. - **With 0.3.0 or older, or a new install:** download the DMG, drag Runlet to Applications, and open it. It's ad-hoc signed, so the first time go to System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security and click **Open Anyway**, or run `/usr/bin/xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Runlet.app`. From then on Runlet updates itself.
Runlet runs on macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later, on Apple silicon and Intel.
## What changed
- **Smaller.** Stable releases now leave out the debugging symbols of Runlet, the `runlet` command, and PHPantom. On disk Runlet goes from 327 to 254 MB. The download goes from 102 to 92 MB (zip) or from 160 to 145 MB (DMG). Nothing else changes. Betas keep their symbols, so testers' crash logs stay readable. - **Website.** [runletapp.dev](https://runletapp.dev) now covers 0.4.0's databases, Redis and MongoDB, code navigation, and in-app updates.
The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/v0.4.2/CHANGELOG.md). `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums of the DMG and zip.

item.title: Runlet 0.4.1
item.description:
Runlet 0.4.1 runs on **macOS 15 (Sequoia)** and later, not only macOS 26 and later.
## Install or update
- **On macOS 26 or later, with 0.4.0 (or beta 7 or 8):** use **Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…** and choose **Install and Relaunch**. - **On macOS 15, or coming from 0.3.0 or older:** download the DMG, drag Runlet to Applications, and open it. It's ad-hoc signed, so the first time go to System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security and click **Open Anyway**, or run `/usr/bin/xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Runlet.app`. From then on Runlet updates itself.
## What changed
- **macOS 15 support.** Nothing in Runlet needed macOS 26 except one system call, which now has a fallback. Runlet's own PHP, PHPantom, Mago and Sparkle already ran on macOS 15. On macOS 15, Runlet shows its classic icon instead of the Liquid Glass one. Tested on macOS 15.6.1 with no PHP installed: Runlet downloaded its own PHP and ran the Laravel sandbox. - **Updates on macOS 15.** From this release on, update-feed entries say macOS 15, so the in-app updater offers new versions there too. - **README.** It no longer says that Runlet doesn't update itself or check for updates. - **Development.** The package tests run in parallel in about 70 seconds instead of six minutes, with `scripts/test.sh fast|full` (add `-v` to list each test).
Everything else is as in [0.4.0](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/releases/tag/v0.4.0). The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/v0.4.1/CHANGELOG.md). `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums of the DMG and zip.

item.title: Runlet 0.4.0
item.description:
Runlet 0.4.0 brings databases beyond your application's own connection, Redis and MongoDB, and in-app updates.
## Install or update
- **From 0.3.0 or older (and 0.4.0 betas 1–6):** download the DMG, drag Runlet to Applications to replace the old copy, and remove the quarantine flag as in the readme's First launch. It's ad-hoc signed, so on first launch right-click Runlet and choose Open, or allow it in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security. - **From 0.4.0 beta 7 or 8:** use **Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…** and choose **Install and Relaunch**. - **From now on,** Runlet updates itself. **Settings ▸ General ▸ Updates** has the channel: Stable (releases only) or Beta (pre-releases too).
## Databases
- **Saved connections:** MySQL and MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server and custom DSNs, with passwords in the Keychain. They can be read-only, go through an SSH profile's tunnel, or connect from this Mac (Runlet picks the first local PHP that has the driver). - **SQL tabs:** bound parameters with a parameters drawer, Explain plans, Load Next past the 1,000-row cap, every result set, CSV export of a whole query and CSV import, and Stop on the database server. - **The Database pane:** the schema explorer with Show Definition, Browse Table with reviewed row edits, Show Relations (the foreign key diagram), and a Server section with version, sizes and sessions. - **Redis tabs:** saved and application connections, a key browser, a server panel, and completion for commands, options and keys. - **MongoDB tabs:** queries as structured JSON, collection reads, and Load More. - **Builders** (View ▸ Show Builder, ⌥⌘B) for Redis commands and MongoDB queries. Both write text into the editor and never run anything. - **The Connection Manager:** every open connection, SSH tunnel and run, including runs queued for a free slot. - **Importing saved connections from TablePlus,** behind a feature flag.
## Also new
- **Code navigation in PHP tabs:** Go to Definition (F12), Find References (⇧F12), code actions (⌥↩), inlay hints and folding. - **Log viewer** (View ▸ Logs, ⌘L): a target's log files, parsed and watched, and a container's or server's logs after Follow. - **Dry Run:** runs a PHP tab inside database transactions that are always rolled back. MySQL statements that would commit at once are refused. - **Source excerpts in error cards,** and expandable stack frames. - **The snippet API:** `\Runlet\notice()`, `warning()` and `error()` cards, with a reference. - **Mail:** WordPress mail in the run inspector, with Intercept Mail; the mail chip shows the mail mode and switches it. - **Editor:** Format Code (⌥⇧⌘F), Promote a snippet to an Artisan command or test, notifications for long runs, and moving and duplicating lines (⌥↑/⌥↓, ⇧⌥↑/⇧⌥↓). - **A guided tour** on first launch, and **What's New** after updates, with Show Me tours (Help ▸ Show Tour, Help ▸ What's New). - **Runlet's PHP r3** adds ext-mongodb.
The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/blob/v0.4.0/CHANGELOG.md#040--2026-10-05). `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums of the DMG and zip.

item.title: Runlet 0.4.0-beta.8
item.description:
**Pre-release for testing.** Built from `main` at 57a5682 with the version set to 0.4.0 (build 14). Runlet 0.3.0 stays the latest release.
**Updating from beta 7:** use **Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…** (Beta channel) and choose **Install and Relaunch**. Betas 1–6 can't update themselves: install this one by hand, as in the readme's First launch.
## New in beta 8
- **Guided tour** ([#232](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/issues/232)). - **When it shows:** on the very first launch, eight short stops point at the real controls: the target menu, Run, the output, History and snippets, Open Anything, database tabs, the Connection Manager, and Settings. - **Controls:** Back / Next / Skip Tour, with Return and Esc. It never runs code, connects anywhere, or changes data. - **Replay:** **Help ▸ Show Tour**. - **What's New** ([#232](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/issues/232)). - **When it shows:** on the first launch of a newer build, it lists the highlights since the build you last opened, newest first. - **Show Me:** it points at the real control for that feature, for example the builder button, Dry Run or the connection count. - **Reopen or turn off:** **Help ▸ What's New** opens it any time. **Settings ▸ General ▸ Tips** turns it and the first-launch tips off. - **Coming from beta 7:** you see all of 0.4.0, since beta 7 had no What's New to remember what you'd seen. - **Neither one interrupts:** they wait while code runs or you type, and never appear for `runlet mcp`, the self-test, or UI tests.
## Still to check
- **The update from beta 7 to this beta:** - the download and Install and Relaunch; - macOS's App Management and administrator prompts for `/Applications`; - that What's New appears once after the relaunch. - **The guided tour** on a clean data folder. - **From beta 7:** - Logs Follow on a real Docker container and on an SSH host; - Dry Run on your own Laravel and WordPress projects.
Ad-hoc signed: on first launch of a hand-installed copy, right-click Runlet and choose Open, or allow it in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security.

item.title: Runlet 0.4.0-beta.7
item.description:
**Pre-release for testing.** Built from `main` at d5bd5ca with the version set to 0.4.0 (build 13). Runlet 0.3.0 stays the latest release.
**Install this one by hand.** It's the first build that can update itself. Betas 1–6 can't, so download the DMG, drag Runlet to Applications to replace the old copy, and remove the quarantine flag as in the readme's First launch. From now on, **Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…** brings new betas.
## New in beta 7
- **In-app updates** ([#233](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/issues/233)). - **Runlet ▸ Check for Updates…** (also in Open Anything), plus a check at launch and once a day. Each check is one request for the update feed on GitHub, with nothing about you or your Mac. - **Settings ▸ General ▸ Updates:** the channel (Stable, or Beta for betas too) and automatic checks. Betas start on the Beta channel. - **Install and Relaunch** downloads the update and checks its signature against Runlet's key before unpacking it. It then removes the quarantine flag, swaps the app in place and starts the new version. If the new version doesn't start, Runlet puts the old one back and says so. You can also choose **Later** or **Skip This Version**. - No update is offered while code runs. If Runlet's folder needs an administrator, macOS asks for one. If Runlet runs from the DMG, it asks you to move it to Applications first. - **Log viewer** ([#20](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/issues/20)): **View ▸ Logs** (⌘L). - **Local files:** Laravel's, Symfony's and WordPress's logs, and a project driver's `logPaths()`, read from the end and watched live. - **Containers and servers:** a Docker container's output and files, and an SSH host's files, only after **Follow**. Stop closes the remote `tail`. - **Entries:** Monolog stack traces are grouped into their entry. Filter by level or text, or by **Last Run**. File locations open like error-card frames. - **Dry Run** ([#13](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/issues/13)): the **Dry Run** toolbar button of a PHP tab, also in **Run ▸ Dry Run (Roll Back Database Changes)**. - It runs the tab inside database transactions that are always rolled back: Laravel, Doctrine, WordPress `$wpdb`, and PDO. A **Dry run** card says what was rolled back. - **Refused before they run:** MySQL and MariaDB statements that would commit at once (DDL, `TRUNCATE`, `LOCK TABLES`, `START TRANSACTION`), on Laravel, Doctrine and WordPress connections. On a plain PDO connection, Runlet warns and starts a new transaction. - **A transaction that can't begin** stops the run before anything runs on that connection. - **Source excerpts in error cards** ([#8](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/issues/8)). - Error cards show about five lines around the failing line, and a **Thrown in** file when it isn't the snippet. - Stack frames with source have a ▸ that shows their lines. - **Move and duplicate lines** ([#234](https://github.com/filipac/runlet/issues/234)): ⌥↑ / ⌥↓ move lines and ⇧⌥↑ / ⇧⌥↓ duplicate them. They're in **Edit ▸ Lines**.
## Still to check
- **The updater, end to end:** - an update from this beta to the next one; - installing into `/Applications`, including macOS's App Management and administrator prompts. - **Logs:** Follow on a real Docker container and on an SSH host. - **Dry Run** on your own Laravel and WordPress projects. - **From beta 6:** - the TablePlus import against real connections; - Redis and MongoDB against real servers; - PHPantom navigation on Docker and SSH projects.
Ad-hoc signed: on first launch, right-click Runlet and choose Open, or allow it in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security.
